doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: Old friend Ellery Mays calls Eddie
summary: Ellery Mays phones Eddie, recalling the 25-cent club, his last New Orleans job; Eddie says he is very happy with Pete's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I'd like to talk to Eddie Miller, please.
Good. Here he is. How are you?
Eddie?
Yes.
This old friend of yours, Ellery Mays.
Oh, how are you, Ellery? Gee, I haven't seen you in many years.
On the radio just now, that solo was beautiful.
Well, thank you very much. How you been, Ellery?
All right. I didn't think you'd remember me.
Oh, I'll never forget you.
Yeah?
I'll never forget you. I'll never forget you.
I'll see you over the 25-cent club on a bike example.
That's right. That was the last place I worked in New Orleans before I left town.
Is that a fact?
Sure.
Yeah. It's years ago, huh?
Yes, sir. How are you doing? Fine? Just great. You can't...
You're with Pete and I, Regler?
Yeah. I couldn't be any happier, especially with Pete and the guys. You know, this is utopia.
That's being the right, huh?
Right, right. Why don't you try to come in and see me at the club?
I sure will, Eddie. Nice talking to you.
Sure good to hear from you, Ellery.
Okay, boy.
Bye.
